# Executive Summary

Germline variant interpretation in R ends the same way in every lab. An analyst has a table of filtered variants and needs to match it against ClinVar, gnomAD, Ensembl VEP and protein resources. Each resource names a variant differently, accepts a different query, and returns a different table shape. The analyst writes the same normalization, joining and bookkeeping code again, and that code rarely records which release of which resource produced each annotation. Six months later nobody can say why a variant was called benign.

tidyvar will be an R package that gives these tables one shape and one identity: a variant table built on tibble that round-trips with the VRanges class from VariantAnnotation, GA4GH Variation Representation Specification (VRS) 2.0 identifiers so variants join exactly across resources and genome builds, adapters that annotate the table from ClinVar, gnomAD, Ensembl VEP, MyVariant.info, UniProt and local files, and a provenance record on every annotated column. Today no R implementation of VRS exists, and the tidyomics ecosystem has no variant package.

I work on variant interpretation for rare and undiagnosed disease at the Center for Computational Genomics and Data Science at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, and my lab will use the package on real case reviews from its first release. The package builds on three released R packages maintained by contributor Samuel Bharti: bioclients (clients for 29 biological web services with one table shape), biohttp (caching, rate limits and retries) and biobouncer (validation of variant notation). I ask for 10,000 USD over eight months in three milestones, each shipping a tagged release on r-universe: the variant table and VRS identifiers, the adapters and provenance, then documentation and a Bioconductor submission.
